en.headline: Twelve cars punctured by nails on Tsing Yi North Coastal Road
en.dek: Police collected 16 nails after drivers heading towards Lantau reported blowouts near an Environmental Protection Department emissions site on Wednesday evening.
body: Police classified a Wednesday evening incident on Tsing Yi North Coastal Road as criminal damage after 12 vehicles suffered punctured tyres. Officers were called at 8.29pm and collected 16 nails from the carriageway. No injuries were reported and no one has been arrested.

Drivers travelling towards Lantau said they hit the nails near the Environmental Protection Department portable emissions measurement site during the evening peak. Photographs circulated among motorists showed nails picked up from the road and at least one taxi stopped with a damaged tyre.

Police have not said how the nails came to be on the road. A similar cluster of punctures on Tolo Highway near Tai Po South in mid-September was linked by officers and Highways Department staff to construction nails that had to be cleared from several lanes.

zh.headline: 青衣北岸公路16枚鐵釘 12車爆胎
zh.dek: 周三晚往大嶼山方向近環保署廢氣實測室對開，警方檢獲16枚鐵釘，列刑事毀壞，暫未有人被捕。
body: 警方將周三晚上青衣北岸公路的爆胎事件列作刑事毀壞。晚上八時二十九分接報後，到場在行車路檢獲16枚鐵釘，共12輛車輪胎被刺穿。事件無人受傷，暫未有人被捕。
多名司機當時沿青衣北岸公路往大嶼山方向行駛，駛至環保署便攜式廢氣測量系統實測室對開時懷疑輾過鐵釘。網上流傳照片顯示有人在路面拾起釘子，亦有的士停在路旁處理爆胎。
警方未有說明鐵釘如何出現在路面。九月中吐露港公路近大埔南出口亦曾有多車懷疑被工程用鐵釘刺穿輪胎，警員當時聯同路政署清理後恢復行車。
